主要内容: Toshiba America Electronic Components, Inc. (TAEC) announced its newest 1.12-micron CMOS image sensor (CIS), the T4KA7, for high-end smartphones and mobile handsets with 20-megapixel resolution. The sensor has an optical size of 1/2.4 inch and enables camera modules with a z-height of 6mm or less. It offers a frame rate of 22 fps at full resolution, an 83% improvement over its previous 20MP sensor. The T4KA7 supports advanced digital zoom with minimal image deterioration and includes mapped couplet correction via 16Kbit OTP memory. It joins Toshiba's 8MP and 13MP CIS solutions, targeting high-end and midrange devices. The 13MP T4K82 enables 240 fps HD video, while the 8MP T4KA3 targets 720p resolution with 240 equivalent fps. Sample shipments began last month, with pricing at just under US$20 (2,000 Yen), and mass production planned for February 2015. Yole Developpement forecasts a 10% CAGR for the CMOS image sensor market, reaching US$13 billion by 2018, driven by mobile, automotive, industrial, and medical imaging applications.
